practice.prompt: Find the arithmetic mean of 2, 4, and 9.
practice.solution: The total is 15 across 3 values, so 15/3=5.

practice.prompt: Find the mean of the data set 3, 7, 8, 10.
practice.solution: The sum is 28 and the count is 4; 28/4=7.

practice.prompt: Find the mean of 1, 1, 5, 9. Count repeated values.
Find the mean of the five consecutive even values 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
practice.solution: Their sum is 30; 30/5=6. The center of this evenly spaced list is also 6.

practice.prompt: A runner logs 12, 16, and 20 km on three days. Find the mean daily distance in km.
practice.solution: Total distance 48 km divided by 3 days gives 16 km per day.

practice.prompt: Four numbers have a mean of 9. What is their total?

practice.solution: Sum 55 divided by five observations gives 11.

practice.prompt: Three test scores are 80, 90, and 100. Find the mean score.
The mean of 3, 7, 11, and x is 9. Find x.
practice.solution: Four values need total 4×9=36. The known values sum to 21; x=36−21=15.

practice.prompt: The five values 2, 4, 6, 8, x have a mean of 7. Find x.
practice.solution: Target sum is 5×7=35. Known sum is 20, so x=15.

practice.prompt: A frequency table lists value 2 once, value 4 twice, and value 8 once. Find the mean.
Four students average 10 points and six students average 15 points. Find the mean for all ten students.
practice.solution: Group totals are 4×10=40 and 6×15=90; combined mean=130/10=13.

practice.prompt: The mean of five measurements rises from 12 to 15. By how much does their total increase?
practice.solution: The total rises from 5×12=60 to 5×15=75; increase=15.

practice.prompt: Six values have a mean of 8. One value, 20, is removed. Find the mean of the remaining five.
practice.solution: Original total=6×8=48. Remaining total=28; remaining mean=28/5=5.6.

practice.prompt: The five numbers 4, 6, 10, 12, x have a mean of 10. Find x.
One group of five has mean 8; another group of three has mean 16. Find the combined mean.

test.prompt: Five measurements have a mean of 12. Find their total.
The mean of 5, 9, 11, x is 10. Find x.
test.solution: Four values must total 40; 5+9+11=25, so x=15.

test.prompt: Six values have mean 14 and four values have mean 9. Find the combined mean.
test.solution: Totals 84 and 36 sum to 120 over ten values; mean=12.

explanation.heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
explanation.body: Compute and interpret an arithmetic mean; recover missing values, work with frequency tables, and combine groups correctly.

explanation.heading: CORE IDEA
explanation.body: The mean is an equal-share value: redistribute the total equally across all observations without changing the total.

explanation.heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
explanation.body: An observation is one recorded value. The count n includes repeated observations. The sum is the total of all values.

explanation.heading: CORE RULE
explanation.body: Arithmetic mean = (sum of all observed values) ÷ (number of observed values). For n values, total = n × mean.

explanation.heading: HOW IT WORKS
explanation.body: Add every value, count every observation, divide sum by count, and label units where appropriate. Recheck by multiplying the mean by n.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — BASIC
explanation.body: For 4, 6, 8, sum=18 and n=3, so mean=18/3=6. Check: 3×6=18.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — REPEATS
explanation.body: For 1, 1, 5, 9, sum=16 and n=4, so mean=4. Both 1s must be counted.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — MISSING VALUE
explanation.body: The mean of 3, 7, 11, x is 9. Required total=4×9=36; known total=21; x=15.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — FREQUENCY TABLE
explanation.body: Value 2 occurs once, 4 twice, 8 once. Weighted total=2+8+8=18; total frequency=4; mean=4.5.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — COMBINED GROUPS
explanation.body: Four scores average 10 and six average 15. Combined total=4×10+6×15=130; count=10; mean=13, not 12.5.

explanation.heading: TRANSFORMATIONS
explanation.body: Adding c to every value increases the mean by c; multiplying every value by k multiplies the mean by k. An outlier can pull the mean strongly.

explanation.heading: COMMON MISTAKES
explanation.body: Do not divide by the number of distinct values when there are repeats. Do not average group means unless the groups have equal counts.

explanation.heading: EXAM STRATEGY
explanation.body: For missing values, write target total=n×mean first. For combined groups, compute each group's total and divide by combined count.

explanation.heading: QUICK CHECK
explanation.body: Find the mean of 2, 4, 9 (5). Four numbers have mean 7: what is their total? (28). If 10 is divided by 5, what is the mean? (2).

explanation.heading: LESSON RECAP
explanation.body: Mean=total/count; total=mean×count. Use frequencies as weights and group sizes as weights when combining samples.

explanation.heading: NEXT STEP
explanation.body: Try all 18 practice questions, check the 18 aligned worked solutions, and submit the five-question lesson test.

english.title: Objective
english.narration: The arithmetic mean is a fair-share value: total divided by the number of observations.

english.title: Core formula
english.narration: Add every value, then divide by how many values there are. Include duplicates.

english.title: Example one
english.narration: Four, six, and eight total eighteen. Divide by three to get six.

english.title: Example two
english.narration: One, one, five, and nine total sixteen across four values. The mean is four.

english.title: Why repeats count
english.narration: Repeated values are separate observations. Never divide by the count of distinct numbers.

english.title: Reverse the mean
english.narration: If four values average nine, their total is thirty-six. Multiply mean by count.

english.title: Find a missing value
english.narration: Three, seven, eleven, and x average nine. Total thirty-six, known sum twenty-one, so x equals fifteen.

english.title: Frequency tables
english.narration: Multiply each value by its frequency, add the products, then divide by total frequency.

english.title: Combined groups
english.narration: Four people average ten and six average fifteen. Weighted total one hundred thirty divided by ten is thirteen.

english.title: Mean and outliers
english.narration: An extreme value changes the total and can move the mean considerably.

english.title: SAT strategy
english.narration: For missing data, compute the target sum first. For grouped data, weight each mean by its group size.

english.title: Recap
english.narration: Mean equals sum over count. Practice the eighteen problems, review solutions, then take the five-question test.

arabic.title: الهدف
arabic.narration: المتوسط الحسابي هو مجموع القيم مقسوماً على عددها، وهو يمثل التوزيع المتساوي للمجموع.

arabic.title: القانون
arabic.narration: اجمع كل القيم ثم اقسم على عدد المشاهدات، واحسب القيم المتكررة كل مرة تظهر فيها.

arabic.title: مثال أول
arabic.narration: الأعداد أربعة وستة وثمانية مجموعها ثمانية عشر، وبالقسمة على ثلاثة يكون المتوسط ستة.

arabic.title: مثال ثان
arabic.narration: واحد وواحد وخمسة وتسعة مجموعها ستة عشر، وعدد القيم أربع، لذلك المتوسط أربعة.

arabic.title: التكرار مهم
arabic.narration: القيمة المتكررة تمثل أكثر من مشاهدة، فلا تقسّم على عدد القيم المختلفة فقط.

arabic.title: عكس القانون
arabic.narration: إذا كان متوسط أربع قيم تسعة فإن مجموعها يساوي أربعة في تسعة، أي ستة وثلاثين.

arabic.title: إيجاد المجهول
arabic.narration: متوسط ثلاثة وسبعة وأحد عشر وسين يساوي تسعة. المجموع المطلوب ستة وثلاثون، إذن سين يساوي خمسة عشر.

arabic.title: جدول التكرار
arabic.narration: اضرب كل قيمة في تكرارها، واجمع النتائج، ثم اقسم على مجموع التكرارات.

arabic.title: دمج المجموعات
arabic.narration: أربعة أشخاص متوسطهم عشرة وستة أشخاص متوسطهم خمسة عشر. المجموع الكلي مئة وثلاثون، والمتوسط ثلاثة عشر.

arabic.title: القيم المتطرفة
arabic.narration: القيمة البعيدة جداً تؤثر في المجموع وقد تغيّر المتوسط الحسابي بشكل ملحوظ.

arabic.title: استراتيجية الامتحان
arabic.narration: عند وجود قيمة مجهولة احسب المجموع المطلوب أولاً، وعند دمج مجموعتين استخدم عدد عناصر كل مجموعة.

arabic.title: الخلاصة
arabic.narration: المتوسط يساوي المجموع على العدد. حل ثمانية عشر سؤال تدريب، وراجع الحلول، ثم اختبر نفسك بخمسة أسئلة.
